Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Tiered credit structure to cover expansion ahead of renewal

Hi Ben,

Congrats on the recent product rollout — appreciate the update on the increased call volume. Given the usage ramp you mentioned, we ran a couple of scenarios for how Valence could add capacity mid-contract while keeping the renewal simple. Attached is a short workbook with three credit/tier options that smooth costs across quarters and preserve unit economics for both sides.

High-level options inside:
- Option A: One-time top-up credit applied immediately, prorated against next invoice.
- Option B: Tiered credits (Q1/Q2 ramp) with a small uplift to committed capacity at renewal.
- Option C: Bridge credit (6 months) to absorb burst spend, then re-evaluate at renewal.

If you like, we can review the numbers with your procurement and finance folks — I included Monica in case we need to coordinate legal/terms. Would you be available for a 30-min call this week?

Thanks,
Ben

Attachments: Valence_Tiered_Credit_Options_v1.xlsx, Proposal_Redwood_Valence_Mar2026.pdf

Hi Ben — thanks for the note and for looping procurement. I pulled together the effective unit price table you asked for and added a short explanation of how the bridge/top-up flows through billing. See the attached spreadsheet. Quick summary here:

- If Valence takes Option B (tiered credits), the effective per-unit rate drops ~18% at Tier 2 once the bumped commit is accepted at renewal.
- For a mid-contract top-up (Option A), we apply a one-time credit that appears as a line item on the next invoice; no invoice reissue required. We can net that against usage for the billing period.
- For Option C (bridge credit), we cap exposure for 6 months while you hit the new baseline; the bridge is amortized monthly to match usage patterns.

Two asks from our side before legal and finance draft the amendment:
1) Confirm target annualized commit after the Q1 ramp (this determines the renewal commit step).
2) Confirm whether Valence prefers invoice consolidation (single PO) or separate line items per quarter.

I can do a quick review call Wednesday morning; propose 11:00am PT. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short one-pager for procurement.

—Monica

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Price structure suggestion for Valence - bridge proposal

Internal note — looping finance conversation into thread. I recommend we offer a short-term bridge credit (Option C) with the following guardrails:

- Bridge length: 6 months, amortized monthly.
- Maximum bridge exposure: 20% of the anticipated annualized commit (this caps financial risk).
- If Valence commits to the bumped baseline at renewal, we convert 50% of the bridge into a permanent commit credit; the remainder is applied as a one-time settlement credit.

Evelyn — can you confirm operational lead time for capacity increases and whether we can guarantee the 4–6 week provisioning window Maya asked about? If not, we should set explicit fallback latency SLAs for burst periods.

Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Tiered credit structure to cover expansion ahead of renewal

Thanks all — after the call and internal review we can proceed with Option C as a starting point if Valence is comfortable with the conversion mechanics below:

- 6-month bridge credit, amortized monthly, cap at 20% of projected annualized spend.
- At renewal, if Valence confirms the higher baseline, 50% of the bridge converts into committed credit applied to the new annual contract; remaining 50% is applied as a one-time invoice credit.
- We will consolidate invoices under a single PO as requested.
- Provisioning lead time: Evelyn confirmed 5 weeks for dedicated capacity in the us-west region; burst fallback to nearest available pool if region capacity constrained.

Next steps:
1) I’ll share an updated proposal PDF and an amendment draft for your procurement team by EOD Tuesday.
2) Procurement to confirm PO approach and any specific invoice fields needed for AP.
3) If procurement agrees, Legal will run a short redline and we’ll route for signature.

Appreciate the collaboration — will follow up with the paperwork.

—Monica
